reviews.text: Reed Flute Cave is a popular attraction located not far from downtown Guilin. From the parking area, visitors need to walk uphill for about 10 minutes to reach the entrance. If walking is difficult, there is a small monorail service available to take you up. Inside the cave, it is quite dark and there are many stairs, so visitors should walk carefully. It’s not recommended to take photos or videos while walking for safety reasons. The cave features a fascinating variety of stalactites and stalagmites in unusual shapes. Some formations resemble animals and objects such as tigers, lions, mushrooms, broccoli, and even a hermit figure. The natural rock formations make the cave both mysterious and impressive.

This cave was one of the best caves I’ve ever been to. Absolutely breathtaking inside, with stunning formations and lighting that make every section feel magical. What made it even more special was knowing that some scenes from the Monkey King movie were filmed here, which gave the visit an extra wow factor—especially for fans of the story. Well organised, easy to walk through, and truly unforgettable. A must-see experience if you’re in the area.

Worthy of a visit if you in Guilin, you probably need about 2 hours including wait time and snack/gift shop. There are quite a lot of steps to get to the entrance, no problem for most able bodied people - worth thinking about if you have kids or mobility issues. However you can hire a sedan chair ride for RMB300 (each way) if needed to get to the entrance. But you also need to consider the many slippery steps and low headroom within some parts of the cave. The cave itself is impressive if you haven't visited a cave before. We didn't feel it was any better than others we have seen elsewhere. The coloured lighting makes the atmosphere somewhat artificial to other caves we have visited and gives a make believe type feeling. To be honest we would rather see a cave in a more natural light. Our guide pointed out several shapes on the cave walls, including a REED and a FLUTE, hence the name. To be honest you needed a vivid imagination to see these shapes, in fact you could see whatever you wanted them to be. Crowd control was not particularly great - too many people pushing and shoving, so be careful! The most annoying thing was the very loud tour guides using megaphones or microphones with loud speakers. Apparently the cave management are trying to get these stopped and encourage tour guides to use whisper headsets instead! Overall a good experience, just a little chaotic and noisy.

Beautiful cave. The lights definitely make a difference with how you view each stalagmite. We had a tour guide that was able to tell us a story of each view. If that is an option for you to have then it’s worth it. There was also an option to have people carry you up to the caves, through the caves and back to your transportation on a chair if you’re not mobile. It cost 300RMB.

One of the amazing things you can see in Guilin. It is astonishing to see how nature forms these interesting stalactites and stalagmites. A few of them resemble animals, people, fruits, vegetables and landscapes. The way they are lit also makes it even prettier. I would not recommend this for people with mobility problems because it involves quite a bit of walking up and down stairs. The men's toilet was also special. The urinals are enclosed in glass and you can have a nice view while peeing 😁 Make sure you visit this place if you are in Guilin. Not to be missed.
Nice cave walk exploration here to spend 1hr in it. Recommended. But beware that the floor can be wet. The cable car ride is just not worth it. Better walk up and down on your own.
One of the Top limestone caves. The entrance is 90 RMB. The tour takes between 75-120 Minutes. Some Stalactites are more than 30m high. It is a great experience

We made the right decision to take the tram up to the entrance to the cave even though this is a separate cost apart from the entrance ticket. There are 2 prices to the entrance ticket. The more expensive one basically includes an entrance fee to a specific section in the reed cave itself. Can do without, I find nothing spectacular in there, it's just some manmade photo spots with some artificial lightings. The cave was wet and could be slippery so wear suitable shoes with good friction. Interesting guided tour (included in entrance ticket) in Mandarin. I think it's worth a visit if you're in Guilin for a couple of days.

I’ve always loved admiring natural scenery, and this time I had the chance to visit Reed Flute Cave. It’s a well-known karst cave relatively close to the city center and has even hosted several national leaders. Inside, you’ll find an incredible variety of stalactites, stalagmites, stone pillars, curtains, and flowers—each with unique shapes and truly spectacular. Thankfully, it wasn’t too crowded on the day I visited, and since the cave is quite spacious, I could take my time to enjoy the sights and snap photos. Just a heads-up: you need to purchase a ticket to enter. A must-visit for nature lovers!
The whole visit took us about one and half hour to finish. The cave is big, but the trail is relatively short. In terms of the features, it was not as rich as other caves we visited.

Rated a AAAA scenic site, this beautiful cave system filled with stalactites and stalagmites. The additional lighting makes the natural aspects look even more beautiful. It does get quite hot and crowded in the caves. The stairs do get quite steep and it does require a decent level of fitness to get through. Definitely worth the visit.

Pretty cool spot! The place was easy to navigate and the cave was cool but I feel there's a lot of these worldwide and this doesn't really stand out from the others. Definitely worth checking out though.
A great place to visit to see these wonderful caves. The scenery outside is equally stunning and offers a great vista.

This was by far the most beautiful cave I have seen in my entire life, and I have visited many. The way they have placed the lights here just feels like a trippy dream. Every step you take feels magical. Don't miss this cave when you come to Guilin area!
Nice place, but totally skippable. The colored lights make it a bit trashy, and there is no highlight really worth the visit unless you are in love with caves.

Quite a big cave in Guilin. Beautiful formation inside the cave, however I feel that too much colourful lighting installed inside the cave, making it doesnt look natural. Entrance to the cave is per group of about 20-50 people which they will arrange 20-30mins apart between group to avoid overcrowding. You will be taken by the local cave tour guide which will guide and explain as you follow him/her exploring inside the cave. There is a carriage available for those who cannot climb stairs or have limited accessibility, with a fee or RMB300. English speaking tour guide is available at certain timing, twice a day. You can find a travel agent to book your ticket in advance, better rates than what you will pay at the cave ticket office.

This is an attraction you’ll want to see. It’s about an hour once you’re in the cave with the tour guide. It’s like most of caves except this one they used colored lights to make the entire cave look colored. Apparently there are many spots here where they shot journey to the west as well.

Worst part about going here was the staff at the admissions gate. They were refusing to honor the senior fare despite the website clearing stating "valid ID OR Guangxi ID" multiple staff members took screenshots of my phone asking where the ticket was purchased from and asking what website. The worst experience I've ever had after purchasing on trip.com. never has this happened before. Honestly, those women need to learn more about customer service. One of them even followed us into the gift shop after we finished going through thr cavern. In terms of the cave itself, vast room which was amazing to see. Definitely make it a part of your trip to Guilin. The different formations of stones and water was cool. There was one that looked like a goldfish and another of a lion.

I came to Guilin and went to the Reed Flute Cave at the end of October 2018. When I arrived at the bus location, I had to park at the parking location located below. We can climb up on foot or take the train. The Reed Flute Cave is a cave that is formed naturally but requires a very long time. The view of the stone in the cave is given a very beautiful colorful lights. The air outside and inside the cave is very cool. We have to go up and down stairs to walk down the cave. Then prepare yourself and maybe be able to bring water in a bottle because the cave that must be passed is quite long. Inside also at certain times there is a short film projected onto the rock and very good. If we come there with a local guide, they can tell fairy tales about stones that can resemble several shapes.

Very cool the way the lighting was in a bunch of areas of the cave. Can be a little tricky taking pictures here with all the different colors and ways it might come out on your camera/phone. Very crowded. Hard not to take a picture without anyone in front of you. Overall a good time for the families and friends.

Very nice cave, very beautiful lighting. A bit commercial, but there are really nice spots to take photos. Recommend booking a private guide who can explain the history in English, since the staff cannot speak English. In my opinion, it is not the best place in Guilin, but if you are in Guilin and have some free time, it is worth visiting 😊

This place was amazing. The lighting on the caves were stunning. Totally worth a visit. Also our of the caves there was a dude doing hand paintings. These were gorgeous and we bought one. Definitely worth checking out too.

Visited Oct 2015 The Reed Flute Cave is a landmark and tourist attraction in Guilin, Guangxi, China. The cave got its name from the type of reed growing outside, which can be made into flutes. Reed Flute Cave is filled with a large number of stalactites, stalagmites and other rock formations. Inside, there are more than 70 inscriptions written in ink, which can be dated back as far as 792 AD in the Tang dynasty. It was rediscovered in the 1940s by a group of refugees fleeing the Japanese troops. Nowadays, multicolored lighting artificially illuminates the cave. The Reed Flute Cave is filled with various stalactites and stalagmites, which are named according to what they look like and the legends surrounding them, Crystal Palace, Fish Tail Peak, and Dragon Pagoda. One giant stalactite is said to have been the magic spear of the Dragon King, used by the Monkey King Sun Wukong in the Chinese Buddhist classic, Journey to the West. I got Anne a really nice egg / egg cup for her collection from here.

A nice experience. It's about a 30 minute slow walk through the cave. The air is cool and the floors are wet and slippery. Take your water bottle and wear good walking shoes. I went with a tour group and they had a short movie playing across the limestone walls/ceiling. There's also a photo booth within the cave where you can get your photo taken by the cave photographer and printed out. The cave guide spoke good English and pointed out limestones formed like snowman, Christmas trees, local vegetables, mushrooms, etc.

Amazing experience here. But it IS a tourist spot so there will be many people trying to sell you things. My group was also given a coupon where we can choose a oyster and get its pearl. If the pearl is not deformed, then you just have to pay RMB 30 to make it into a necklace.
Worth going - walk through on your own or read guide online (if English is first language). Didn’t take too long, beautiful gardens and spaces outside around the cafes too!

It's interesting to do one of these, but Guilin is filled with caves and caves and more LED-lit-up rainbow-colored caves. That being said the Reed Flute is one of the more famous ones and worth the trek through. I mean after all, Nixon was here.

Don't come here. It has nothing as advertised. The cave is ugly. So many other caves in the world better. It's small and has nothing for you to get wow. You buy an entry ticket then they asked you if you want to buy an extra ticket for the so-called "secret garden". You get in, everything is underwhelmed. Then you go to that "secret garden" where they have some laser lights of dragon head, and that's it. I would call it a scam. And not finishing yet, you need to be careful to get scams by the shop when you exit. They tried to trap you to buy Chinese medicine and some herbal stuff. They are terrible. My friend got scammed buying things from them. Extremely expensive. How a government's approved place let them do that? And why this cave is a recommended to visit for Guilin? So bad. Waste money and time.
Good for sightseeing. They use lighting to enhance the ambience. The air inside however, gave me a headache.

A fun cave, though it's not in as natural a state as others I've been in. Lots of lights and paths to make it accessible for all ages and abilities. The special effects make it fun, though the movie they show is a classic nationalistic propoganda piece!
It's amazing. It's pretty. It would be perfect if the lighting was a bit simpler.

Went during the summer, the cave was cold inside, helped with the summer heat. Did not expect the cave to be so huge, had a wonderful time taking photos and appreciating the tour (although it’s only provided in mandarin at the time I went)
Very scenic with lots of shops and local food shops nearby, great place to spend the day in 桂林!
The tour guide is so professional and very nice. The cave is very beautiful and there are two shows to see in the cave.

Located in Guilin, Guangxi, China, reached after crossing the Li River by dragon boat tour. It is called the Bamboo Flute Cave because the bamboo that grows wild around the cave can be made into a flute. Many stalactites, stalagmites and other large rocks are illuminated with colorful lights making it look very attractive.

Was amazed by their lighting technic to made the cave looks even more majestic. They are quite creative on makin the theme for each stones that created similar enough to resembles something. I was fortunate that i could understand a but of Chinese, otherwise their story plot line was useless. It’s beautiful overall but the price to enter for me is quite expensive.

Very impressive. We came during the winter so it was not crowded. The cave is well paved but not suitable for wheelchairs. The cave has a lot of lights that make it look and feel a bit staged. But the formations are so impressive you overlook the music and weird Swan Lake performance.

It was really a pleasure for me to visit that reed flute cave. You must go there once in your life and watch it ith your whole heart. It's beauty is unlimited. I am very thankful to God for giving me a chance to visit this beautiful cave which has multicolored stalactites and stalagmites.

Not bad, it was more commercialized than the things we usually go for. We were a five-person group, and so we got to explore some parts not accessed by the general public. It became crowded in the main cavern, but then again, it’s China, so that’s to be expected. It would be more interesting if it had been left natural with just headlamps or a few regular lights to light up the dark. The path is fully paved, so it would be easy for someone with mobility issues, just watch for the occasional stairway.

Very disappointing overall experience. The unregulated flow of tourist, cheesy sound effect and unnecessarily bright colorful lights completely disrupted the 180 millions years old ecosystem of the cave. It took away the awe and beauty of such a natural wonder and everything looked too artificial.
Beautiful and colourful cave that is accessible by city bus. Definitely worth a visit!

If you are looking for an "authentic" caving experience, this ain't it. But if you are just looking for a beautiful experience, this is definitely it. The colors and ceiling show were quite stunning, but what really stayed with me was the moment I rounded a corner and found myself on the edge of a monstrous precipice. My heart nearly stopped. It was like looking into the portal to hell. It was a moment or two before I realized I was actually looking at the surface of a shallow reflective pool mirroring the stalactites and red lighting of the ceiling far above. Even after I knew what it was I couldn't help getting acrophobiac twinges every time I looked down at the reflection.

Nice place to visit if you haven't seen a cavern like it. Not enough signage protecting it. Just touching destroys them. Most places don't color them up like this however. I like it overall and the short film on the ceiling they had was worth the wait.

A beautiful cave to see. Issues come with how touristy the place is all around, with people trying to sell you stuff before and after the cave. It is also only operated on a guided tour format, for no free exploration inside. And don't take the monorail to the top of the mountain, it is a waste of money.

It’s a beautiful site worth a visit. I personally like more about more naturally presented caves and frankly wondered if their activities gradually damaging this natural beauty made over years before human history…

Overall not bad. If you're looking for pretty sites (locations) and not for an authentic style cavern, this is a good spot. Pretty lights, opportunities for photos, but heavy-handed on pulling money from the visitors.

Not as good nor as rustic as New Zealand's glow worm cave, but still worth a visit. About an hour long guided tour in Chinese. Difficult to hail taxis; we made arrangements with our taxi driver who ferried us there, for him to wait and pick us up for the return journey.
The tickets are somewhat expensive but I enjoyed the cool temperature in the caves and the LED lighting.

Can't really complain too much since there's no admission cost. But the orangutan exhibit is just sad. Very artificial and the animals just look miserable. Not a single tree or blade of grass in there for the orangutans.

Kids were keen after seeing pictures. It was better than I expected and they sent us in without a group because we didn't speak Mandarin so we enjoyed the cave without a group and it was a cool respite from the heat

So sad to see. They've completely ruined what could have been such a wonder by destroying it to make a commercial tourist trap. Everywhere you looked there where huge stalactights and stalagmites that would have taken thousands of years to form just snapped off to make room for paths, lights, cameras, signs, or anything. There where FAKE stalactights in places (pictured) and a whole section had been destroyed to clear an opening for them to project some garbage chinese propaganda. If you enjoy caving, spelunking or even just anything natural you will hate this. I hate that I gave them any money.

Reed Flute Cave known as “the Palace of Natural Arts” is located in the northwest of Guilin in southern China. According to a legend, Reed Flute Cave got its name because people believed that the reed by the cave’s mouth could be made into flutes. The limestone cave offers a majestic fairyland of stalactites, stalagmites, stone pillars, stone curtains, birds, plants and animals in fantastic shapes and colors.
Beautiful. Must visit. Would be 5 but personally I didn't really like quite so much colourful lighting inside the caves. Good for photos though!

The Reed Flute Cave , also known as "the Palace of Natural Arts” is a landmark and tourist attraction in Guilin, Guangxi, China.It is a natural limestone cave with multicolored lighting and has been one of Guilin’s most interesting attractions for over 1200 years. It is over 180 million years old.
Very over the top bedazzled lights and projections detracted from the already interesting natural structures.
A very enjoyable visit. And I really like the lighting. It shows the rocks in their natural colours. Must be one of the most visited place in Guilin.
It's very nice. Lots of lights to help you see the formations. Admission is a little high in my opinion, but we are happy we did it.

Must go place to visit in Guilin. But I think Hwansun cave환선굴 in south Korea is much better The admission fee is way pricy in China 110cny 환선굴 is way beautiful but entrance costs only 4usd it is huge and it has a fall and river in it the reed flute cave is the best spot in Guilin though 계림에선 갈 만 한곳으로 강추
Great experience. Beautiful lighting accenting the formations. Pretty busy but patience allows you to get moments of some solitude in waves of groups.
Huge cave. Colorful lighting. Worth a visit. Don't miss the short video about the cave showed at the end of the path.
The cave is beautiful, but the service is terrible when you want to get the small version of photo that is included in the ticket but don't want to purchase extra photos
Travel into a deep dark cave and enjoy the natural formations of stalagmites and stalactites..with the additions of colorful lights and some really incredible imagination to see what it is about.
Except when it's crowd this place gives the feeling of the long time need to build such amazing natural view. It's so special to know even Deng Xiaoping has been here.
Great tour! Kids loved it. The tour guide was very knowledgeable. Video on the ceiling was a highlight.
Beautiful limestone caves with dramatic colored lighting. Very enjoyable underground tour.
It's very nice to visit but it's a big tourist atraction, full of chineses tourist. And little expensive but it's still wonderfull.
Terrible loudspeaker voice from staff. Totally annoying. And cheap videos inside. Other way the nature cave would be so great
Fantastic place, never expected it to be so big, well worth a visit if your in Guilin for a holiday
If anything inte the World is awesome, this is it. One of the top sights in my life.

Cette grotte se trouve au nord de Guilin, à 15 min de voiture environ. Nous avons fait appel à un guide privé pour nous emmener à celle-ci. L'entrée coûte 90 ¥ par personne. C'est une jolie grotte où la visite s'étire sur 500 mètres environ. Différentes zones scénarisées avec lumières et parfois du son vous attendent le long de la visite. Notre guide nous a donné beaucoup d'informations. Il faut avoir beaucoup d'imagination pour se représenter les choses et objets que notre guide voyait dans certaines concrétion, stalagmites et autre stalactites. Nous y sommes allé tôt le matin, peu de temps après l'ouverture, il n'y avait pas grand monde. Prévoir 45 minutes de visite.

Cueva enorme, maravillosa, con acceso opcional en mini-tren. Muy bien arreglada, cuidada y sobretodo iluminada. Aunque te obligan a entrar en grupo (chino), una vez dentro puedes desmarcarte e ir por tu cuenta. Dentro del recorrido, encuentras una opción de pago, muy recomendable, con animaciones lumínicas visuales muy espectaculares, vale la pena. Atracción imperdible!!!
不錯的溶洞景點、雖然整體不是很大、但對第一次參觀人來說已經是不錯的初體驗、非常壯觀、也很有特色、該有的特色溶洞都有了、所以一次1個多小時體驗足夠了、就是打車直接上售票處、不要再下面搭35人民幣小火車上來、套路、冤枉錢。

Reed Flute Cave (ถ้ำขลุ่ยอ้อ) ระหว่างทางขึ้นสู่ถ้ำเป็นเหมือนสวนสาธารณะต้องเดินขึ้นไปหรือซื้อตั๋วขึ้นรถราง ไปช่วงเช้าไม่ร้อนมากค่ะ ภายในถ้ำอากาศเย็นสบาย จัดแสดงไฟตรงจุดบริเวณหินงอกหินย้อยได้สวยงาม ดูมีสีสันดีค่ะ ระหว่างทางอาจจะมีน้ำหยดต้องระวังลื่นด้วยนะคะ

Poole km jagu värviliselt valgustatud käike. 180 miljoni aasta tagusest ajast pärinev Roopilli nimeline koobas, mis imelist värvidemängu pakkus. Tõeline loodusekunsti palee. Stalaktiitide ja stalagmiitide moodustumine võtab miljoneid aastaid aega ning nende kummalised ja mitmekesised kujud on kindlasti väärt külastamist. Värvilised tuled loovad tõeliselt maagilised vaated

中国広西チワン族自治区の桂林市にある鍾乳洞で中国の中でも古代に発見されたとても有名な場所です。発見が早かったことから様々な時代の有名人が訪れてはその形を見ていろんな名前をつけていることも大変面白いです。人気の観光名所であることからいつも混み合っていて最低でも1時間程度は並ばないと入ることができません。一つのグループごとに入場する形でガイドが付いて案内をしてくれることでそれについて進むだけで楽しむことができます。外が暑い分中が涼しくゆっくり進みながら自然が作った景色を楽しめます。

Grotta spettacolare e tracciato ben segnato. Costo 90 yuan. Facilmente raggiungibile dal centro con didi o taxi. In un'ora si visita. Se uno ha poco tempo e ha già visto qualche bella grotta italiana qui lo spettacolo di ripropone. Particolare effetto sono le illuminazioni.
Caverna e muito bonita e bem cuidada. A beleza natural somada a cores e luzes dão um cenário incrível.
街の中心から、三路のバスで訪れました。 入場料は、90元。（As of Feb. 2025）いつからかは分かりませんが、以前来た時には無かったモノレールで洞窟の入口近くまで行けるようになっていました。（別途料金35元） 中に入ると、十数名ずつのグループでガイドの説明を聞きながら見学するようになっていましたが、中国語が全く分からないので、集団を離れて自由に見学して回りました。

A barlang a nevét az odakint növő nádfajtáról kapta, amelyből fuvolát lehet készíteni, de a vadmacskák gyakori felbukkanása miatt macskabarlangként is szokták emlegetni. Számos jel utal arra, hogy már az ókor óta Guilin egyik látványossága volt a barlang. 1940-es években fedezték fel újra a japán csapatok elől menekülők. A Nádfuvola-barlang tele van különböző cseppkövekkel és sztalagmitokkal, szikla alakzatokkal, amelyeket aszerint neveztek el, hogy hogyan néznek ki és milyen legendák övezik őket. A barlang belsejében egy kristálytiszta tó található. A barlang ~180 millió éves és 1200 éve látogatják, amiről barlangrajzok is tanúskodnak. Belül több mint 70 falfelirat található. Az eddig felfedezett legkorábbi rajzot 792-ben készítették, a Tang-dinasztia korában. Az U alakú barlang átlagos magassága 10 m és legmagasabb pontja ~ 20 m. Bejárata a tengerszint fölötti 176 méteres magasságban található, a völgy fölött csupán 27 méterre helyezkedik el. Kelet-nyugat irányban hossza eléri az 500 métert, dél-észak irányban a szélessége pedig 50 és 90 m közötti. Az eldugott bejárat elég nagy, mely egy tágas, közel 15 ezer m2 kiterjedésű terembe nyílik. Ennek falai szabálytalanok, számos sziklaüreg tarkítja, a terem délnyugati felén két kisméretű járat található. Az egyik 90 méter hosszú, és folyamatosan emelkedik felfelé. A másik üreg viszont lefelé kanyarog, és olyan mintha a cseppkőbarlangban egy mély szakadék tátongna. Ennek igen fontos szerepe van, hiszen a barlangba zúduló víz ezen keresztül távozik.
桂林的溶洞雖然以銀子岩最有名，但想體驗，又不想坐車太久，可以去蘆笛岩就好，離市區萬象城很近，又有免費解說員講解，五十分鐘的觀光路程，很舒服！可以提早在小程序或是其他平台買票，可能有優惠，但是要在入場前一小時就買好，不能馬上買馬上使用喔

Очень атмосферно! Освещение на высочайшем уровне. Важно отделиться от китайских экскурсий и побыть наедине с пещерой. До этого читал отзывы про толпы туристов. Но в реале группы проходят. И в перерыве между ними только пару самостоятельных туристов

Nada más pagar el ticket, bastante caro por cierto, te abordan para que cojas el tren diciéndote que hay que subir 200 escalones y que la entrada está lejos. No es cierto, no merece la pena coger el tren, es un auténtico timo. Además, pagamos ida y vuelta y cuando fuimos a cogerlo de vuelta nos dijeron que solo habíamos pagado la ida. El camino caminando es precioso, merece la pena el paseo. La cueva demasiado iluminada, demasiados colores. En general, no recomiendo la visita
20241203遊桂林蘆笛巖溶洞景區 團體有安排導覽人員解說 溶洞內的石筍 石乳 石柱景觀被命名為獅嶺朝霞 原始森林 水晶宮等 感覺還真像 出口處的蘆笛巖 芳蓮閣 桃花江畔山水景觀如畫卷 值得一遊

Eine wunderschöne Tropfsteinhöhle! Bunte Kristalle und prächtige Stalagmiten erwarten einem, wenn man in diese Höhle geht. Man braucht etwa eine bis zwei Stunden, um die Höhle zu durchwandern. Man kann zwar entweder alleine oder in der Gruppe rein, aber dahin kommt man nur mit einer Reisegruppe. Auch ist dies ein wunderbarer Ort zum Fotos machen!

구이린 시내에 15분에서 20분 가량 소요되는 reed flute cave입니다. 매표소에 가면 성인 입장료는 90CNY입니다. 그리고 구이린 시내 여섯 곳을 방문 할 수 있는 4day pass를 195CNY를 판매하고 있습니다. 70세 이상의 경우 50%할인을 해준다고 되어 있으나 이 부분은 중국인인 경우에만 해당된다고 합니다. 가이드와 함께 동굴 내를 이동하게 되며 입장하게 되면 신기 찬란한 석회 동굴의 향연이 끝날때 까지 계속 됩니다. 정말 엄청나고 신비로움의 연속입니다. 코스의 중간 정도 오면 수정궁이라는 곳이 나오는데 동굴 내 잔잔한 호수에 그대로 석순들이 그대로 비춰서 그 아름다움은 배가 됩니다. 마지막에 추가 옵션으로 장수 거북이와 함께 사진을 촬영할 수 있는 코스가 있습니다. 꼭 한번 방문해보시길 추천합니다. 다른 석회동굴과 그 규모에서 엄청나게 차이가 납니다.

Reed Flute Cave adalah gua yang sangat indah terletak di pinggiran barat laut Guilin, Guangxi, Cina, 5 km dari pusat kota Guilin. memiliki kedalaman sekitar 240 meter dan panjang 500 meter. Gua ini memiliki berbagai macam stalagmit, stalaktit, pilar batu dan tirai batu yang sangat indah, yang telah terbentuk sejak 180 juta tahun yang lalu. Gua ini juga dikenal sebagai "Istana Seni Alam". Saat berada didalam Reed Flute Cave, pengunjung akan takjub dengan keindahan stalagmit yang berembun. Cahaya pelangi dan susunan formasi alam yang mempesona membentuk keindahan yang mempesona. Danau bawah tanah mengalir di sepanjang gua, memberikan efek pantulan gua yang sangat indah. Bagian dalam Reed Flute Cave adalah pemandangan yang sulit ditemukan bandingannya di belahan bumi lain. Memiliki formasi yang khas dan beberapa dikatakan menyerupai makhluk mitologis atau bangunan modern seperti Patung Liberty . Dibagian luar gua, pengunjung akan menemukan banyak alang-alang yang tumbuh, yang dapat digunakan untuk membuat seruling, dari sinilah nama gua itu berasal. Ada 77 prasasti puisi dan catatan perjalanan di dalam gua, yang menunjukkan popularitasnya selama zaman kuno, dan yang tertua berasal dari Dinasti Tang (792 M) .

La gruta de la flauta de la caña (Lu Di Yan) està llena de estactitas y estalagmitas alcanzando los 16 metros de altura en elgun tramo de la gruta. Se tarda una hora en recorrerla aproximadamente si vamos tranquilos. Llama la atenciòn la iluminaciòn artificial en distintos colores que desluce un poco, pero no es tan disparatado. La abrieron al pùblico desde 1960, pero se hizo popular su visita a partir de los noventa. En la cueva incluyen dos espectaculos audiovisuales por si se desean ver, aunque si vamos ajustados de tiempo no nos perdemos nada fantàstico. Si has visitado otras cuevas o grutas similares no te va a llamar mucho la atenciòn, pero si es la primera vez merece mucho la pena.

Entre los muchos sitios interesantes donde ir en Guilin está esta gruta natural, muy concurrida de turistas, y muy bien acondicionada para realizar un recorrido interior. Únicamente se recomienda llevar calzado apropiado, y tener cuidado con algunas zonas del recorrido que pueden estar encharcadas. Hay peligro de resbalarse. Destaca la iluminación LED, con la que consiguen recrear escenarios muy coloridos...

Traducción del inglés-La cueva de la flauta de caña, también conocida como "el Palacio de las Artes Naturales", es un hito y una atracción turística en Guilin, Guangxi, China. La cueva recibió su nombre del tipo de caña que crece afuera, que se puede convertir en flautas

Gua Suling Buluh, atau "Istana Seni Alam", adalah salah satu daya tarik wisata di Guilin, Guangxi, China. Nama gua ini diambil dari jenis buluh yang tumbuh di luar dan dapat dibuat seruling. Gua Suling Buluh dipenuhi dengan sejumlah besar stalaktit, stalagmit, dan formasi batuan lainnya yang konon cantiknya luar biasa. Konon ditemukan pada tahun 1940 oleh pengungsi yang melarikan diri dari Jepang. Setelah didalam, lagi-lagi seperti melihat lukisan cantik yang hidup dengan mata kepala sendiri dengan bentuk batu-batu yang membuat imajinasi berlari dan terbang. Warna-warni spotlight yg direfleksikan / dipantulkan ke batu itu menambah kecantikan dan daya tarik yang mampu membius mata saya. Wajib, kudu, mesti dan Harus masuk bucketlist jika sedang di Quilin ^^.

洞窟内に入って先ず驚いた事は 奇抜と言うか カラフルと云うか 赤,緑,青等の照明ライトが 鍾乳石を照らしておりました｡ 見た目は綺麗に見えますが 鍾乳石が 泣いているように感じました｡ 気の遠くなる年数を要して出来た自然の贈り物は 自然のありのままの姿で見たいです 昼白照明で充分だと思いました。 然し洞窟内には幾つもの広い空間が有り天井から大きな鍾乳石が垂れ下がり 下には大小無数の鍾乳石が立ち並ぶ情景は 見応えがあります｡ 鍾乳洞の規模は山口県の秋芳洞よりは小さいです｡ 中国人観光客が多く来ており 周囲を気にせず写真を撮る人達、大きな声でおしゃべりをする人達等で ゆっくりと見学出来ませんでした｡ 中国ではマナーという 言葉はないようです｡

基本的にガイド付きでまわります。我々が参加したときはＣＯＶＩＤのせいで中国語ガイドのみだったので子供たちはわりとすぐに飽きてしまっていました。勝手に回っても良いのですが、ライトアップや演出などはガイドと一緒のタイミングでいく必要があります。総じて、すごいスケールの鍾乳洞ですが、純粋に自然の造形美を楽しむというより、いかにも中国的センスのプレゼンテーションも楽しむという気持ちで行く方ががっかりしなくて良いと思います。途中で、記念写真の売り込みなどもあります。
